title: Consideration of hardship
summary: This page explains who can request hardship consideration and provides guidance on the process if you are having difficulty repaying funds from a grant or payment program.
intro:
If your circumstances have changed and you’re finding it difficult to repay funds from a grant or payment program you were found ineligible to receive, you may be able to request hardship consideration.

This option may also be available if you are currently going through a compliance audit and are facing difficult circumstances.

This page outlines who can request consideration of hardship, how to make a request, and what support may be available.
who_can_apply: You are currently going through a compliance audit or other review and are being assessed for financial assistance.
A compliance audit or review has determined you are ineligible for financial assistance, and you are required to repay those funds.
You are experiencing domestic or family violence.
You are experiencing severe financial hardship.
You are experiencing mental health challenges.
You have an intellectual disability or cognitive impairment.
You are experiencing homelessness or risk of homelessness.
what_you_need: Government services that support the community.
Community organizations (such as charities, neighbourhood centres, or support services).
Accredited financial counsellors who have assessed your situation.

how_to_steps.text: confirm that you are seeking hardship consideration
briefly explain which hardship circumstances apply to you (refer to the list above).

faqs.a: You may be eligible if you are going through a compliance audit or review, or if you are required to repay funds because you were found ineligible for financial assistance.

faqs.q: What if I received a debt notice from Revenue NSW?
faqs.a: If you have received a debt notice from Revenue NSW, you must contact them directly for more information.

faqs.q: What types of hardship circumstances are considered?
faqs.a: Circumstances considered include domestic or family violence, severe financial hardship, mental health challenges, intellectual disability or cognitive impairment, and homelessness or risk of homelessness.
